t: #2255 Count Prefixes of a Given String
o: We simply count how many entries of words appear at the beginning of s. In Example 1, "a", "ab", "abc" are prefixes of "abc" (but "b", "bc" are not), giving 3. In Example 2 both copies of "a" count, giving 2. Constraints are tiny (lengths ≤ 10, up to 1000 words), so direct checking is more than fast enough.
k: A word w is a prefix of s iff len(w) ≤ len(s) and s[0:len(w)] == w.
Duplicates in words must each be counted separately — no deduplication.

a.i: For each word, verify it matches the first len(word) characters of s. Built-in startswith does this in one call.
s: For each word w, if s starts with w, increment count.
a.t: O(total characters of words) — each comparison is bounded by word length.

a.i: Without library helpers, compare word[j] with s[j] for j < len(word); any mismatch disqualifies the word. This shows understanding of what startswith does internally and works in any language.
s: For each word w, assume it is a prefix.
Loop j from 0 to len(w)-1; if w[j] != s[j], mark failed and break.
Add 1 to the answer for each word that never fails.
a.t: O(sum of word lengths) — each word checked character by character.

w: Trivial problem; the interview value is correctness under duplicates and the length guard (a word longer than s cannot be a prefix — startswith handles this implicitly). Follow-up: many queries against a fixed s — build a Trie of prefixes of s and look each word up in O(length).
